paragraphs.text: Hexhaven Academy is the Echoverse 's dystopian version of Strixhaven . Unlike its Multiverse counterpart, Hexhaven has five allied-colored schools. It is the preeminent battlemage academy of the Echoverse.

Jace had learned that the only way to give stability to the Echoverse was to lay its skin atop the bones of the existing Multiverse. The key to this step was understanding the creation of Arcavios — how the collision of two planes had created something new and stable. He also needed a place of abundant magical energy and knowledge to stabilize it. For this purpose, Hexhaven was created as his inner sanctum.

Jace's psychic influence is felt across Arcavios, but it is concentrated around Hexhaven. Surreal and mind-bending creatures wander the plane. Physical reality twists and turns in unexpected ways. Some creatures and people exist in a partial state after being caught in the twisting reality of the plane; shifting creatures hold the forms of two different beings, and many creatures are two-headed.

Hexhaven is a dystopian, regimented military academy, and its students are referred to as "cadets". Cadets are recruited from across the plane, selected by admission officers from children who demonstrate magical aptitude. No cadets are accepted from other planes in the Echoverse. Recreation is limited, as cadets are encouraged to spend their time outside of class running drills. The schools don't have mascots .

After the successful completion of all relevant coursework and training, advanced cadets compete in a final multistage trial to graduate. A group comprised of one cadet from each school enters the dueling arena together to face off against mage hunters and other challenges. Hexhaven graduates primarily work as battlemages, but they can also serve as builders, healers, or advisors for Arcavios's more distant villages. Many serve within their schools as professors or teaching assistants, continuing their academic work and going on assignments for the sphinxes or the Theorist. Those who survive but do not pass their final trial can serve as librarians, mess hall cooks, groundskeepers, and research assistants, but failed students are forbidden from accepting formal magical roles — though some are known to do so discreetly.

Echoverse Arcavios is a plane in the process of being born: dangerously unpredictable and in a state of wild flux. But to its people, it has always been this way. Their memories stretch back generations. The lessons of their past were artificially constructed to endear them to the mindmage himself. Jace's efforts to minimize discordance in the Echoverse influenced the mana alignment of the plane. Instead of snarls of conflicting sources, harmonious mana merged, creating five elder sphinxes at the largest confluence of its leylines.

As the plane took shape, the residual effects of Jace's reality magic manifested as natural disasters. Official histories of Hexhaven assert that the elder sphinxes took pity on the denizens of the plane and offered protection from the elements. The sphinxes began teaching the people of their innate magic. A community of students grew, and the sphinxes formally founded an institution where they oversaw the training of Arcavios's population to ensure their survival.

An immense, impossible tower rises from the plane's largest leyline confluence. This specific collection of leylines is a rich source of magic that fuels the education and training at Hexhaven Academy. The elder sphinx Uldaros Theorix used his reality-bending magic to build the original fortress, keeping the campus out of reach of the mage hunters. The Fatehold campus is located at the base of the tower, metaphorically and literally forming the foundation of Hexhaven. A room at the base of the tower still holds the confluence, and its masonry is worn smooth from the leylines' vibrations. The Theorix campus is located near the top and is the closest to the Theorist's sanctum. From his sanctum, the Theorist can survey and guide his fledgling Multiverse through mage-ring portals. The Theorist siphons the leyline energy concentrated under the tower to fuel his work. He rarely leaves his sanctum, preferring to project mental illusions around the tower to gather information and monitor progress. The Theorist's sanctum contains an orrery depicting the entire Echoverse.

The Theorist's presence and continued wielding of reality-bending magic have warped and twisted the tower into an impossible construct. Walls bend, and floors fold. No matter where you are in the tower, other parts of campus appear at unexpected angles. The hallways don't move, but the tower has a way of disrupting where someone is trying to go. A cadet taking a staircase upward might end up three floors below where they started. Konstrari professors say Hexhaven's campus has a "consciousness of its own". The tower's architecture also incorporates elements of Jace's life and memories, increasing in density as one approaches his sanctum. Doorways and windows resemble his insignia and mage-rings from his home plane of Vryn . Statues of him loom over the tower's occupants.
Hexhaven Academy's campus makes up the lower majority of the Theorist's Tower, with each school inhabiting a different vertical "neighborhood."

Fatehold ( ), school of Future History. These mages predict all possible futures, looking for an optimal end state. They then manipulate the present to change the course of history toward that optimal end point.

Theorix ( ), school of Esoteric Mathematics. These mages achieve power over reality through math and theoretical physics. They twist the rules of reality and explore impossibilities to develop solutions to the world's problems. As a result of dealing with all the mind-bending physics and impossible numbers of the underlying fabric of reality, Theorix cadets tend to go insane.

Stingerquill ( ), school of Painful Words. These mages have figured out how to inflict harm by the use of words. The cadets function as Jace's frontline troops, using verbal magic to cut apart the bodies and souls of their opponents.
Konstrari ( ), school of Constructive Arts. These mages channel creativity and artistic inspiration into the construction of buildings, constructs, and puppet soldiers for Jace's grand project.

Vigorbloom ( ), school of Invasive Healing. These mages can cultivate plants in any substrate, and are tasked with keeping the Hexhaven battle mages alive and fighting. They implant plant materials to heal injuries and fix ailments. As they also experiment on themselves, many students have vines or plants growing out of their skin.

While the five schools take up the majority of Hexhaven Academy's vertical footprint, there are several communal areas around campus that are shared by all. The cadet dormitories, the mess hall, and the Folioplex can all be found near the middle of the tower. The latter is a dimly lit archive for magical research, the Echoverse's version of Strixhaven's Biblioplex . The sphinxes encourage professors to keep all records of experiments conducted, theorems proved, and discoveries made, though this information is tightly controlled. Students in the Folioplex are heavily monitored by figments , statues, and staff. The Theorist has restricted many volumes and sections to ensure that no individual with ill intent can gain access to powerful magic.

The Theorist's reality-bending magic left a wasteland surrounding the campus for nearly a hundred miles. The Eradia, as it is called, is crawling with mage-eating monsters and prone to dangerous distortions of reality. Mage hunters and witchstalkers are found in multitudes, drawn to the powerful magic emanating from the top of the tower. Cadets are occasionally tasked with "clearing" sections of the Eradia for disciplinary reasons.

The Theorist maintains a constant state of surveillance across the Echoverse. One of the many ways he does this is by intentionally projecting his essence into living creatures. Birds are often seen with his hooded face in place of the head. Faceless enforcers and creatures with prominent eyes—with irises in the shape of the Theorist Sigil—surveil and spy on the students and the faculty. Cadets might recognize that the enforcers' uniforms have more in common with Vryn than Hexhaven, but questions about this to the Theorist are summarily silenced.

First-year Hexhaven students wear a common school uniform, and all cadets wear a badge that resembles the Theorist's eye. Their first semester is focused on learning the basics of spellcasting and the flora, fauna, and history of Arcavios. In their second semester, first-years rotate through each of the schools, serving as research assistants and even subjects for more advanced students. Students undertake a series of exams and a trial at the end of their first year. The representatives from each community on Arcavios are invited to gather at Hexhaven's central arena to observe. The Founder Sphinxes select the cadets they wish to enroll based on their exam results, trial performance, and methodology. Once the trial is complete, the induction ceremony begins for successful cadets. However, not all first-years are selected for induction—some don't even complete the trial—and these rejected mages return home to learn non-magical trades.
The existence of the Echoverse and Hexhaven was spoiled in November 2025, a half year in advance, through a survey put out by Wizards of the Coast.
